newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Malaysia says ringgit decline no reason for worry.
newsitem.headline: Malaysia says ringgit decline no reason for worry.

text.p: Malaysia Deputy Prime Minister and Finance Minister Anwar Ibrahim said on Monday that the ringgit's fall against the U.S. dollar last week was no reason for concern.
"There is nothing wrong with the ringgit," Anwar told reporters after inaugurating an Asian banking conference.

Last Wednesday, the ringgit hit a six-month low against the U.S. dollar on rumours that the U.S. was seeking sanctions against Malaysian national oil company Petronas and that Bank Negara was comfortable with the ringgit at the 2.53 level, foreign exchange dealers said.
The U.S. has since said it has not taken or recommended any action against Petronas.
The ringgit closed at 2.5250/60 in Kuala Lumpur last Wednesday. At 0045 GM on Monday, the Malaysian unit was at 2.5285/90 in Kuala Lumpur.
"Could you say it's (fallen) very sharply? I dispute that," Anwar said to reporters, when asked if Malaysia was concerned about the ringgit's fall.
